entities.sub: Delhi HC quashed 2004 and 2005; SC dismissed CBI's late appeal 2018 and the last private appeal 2026
entities.publicRole: Court and investigation record of the 1986 Bofors contract; run beside Rafale by design.
d: Subject: US$285 m contract for 410 155mm howitzers signed 24 Mar 1986 (Rajiv Gandhi government, Congress) [reported]
First public allegation: Swedish Radio, 16 Apr 1987 [reported]
Investigating body: CBI (FIR 22 Jan 1990, RC 1(A)/90; chargesheet 22 Oct 1999) [documented]

Latest stage: all proceedings quashed/discharged (Delhi HC 4 Feb 2004 in part; 31 May 2005 fully for the Hinduja brothers and the Bofors company); SC dismissed CBI's SLP 2 Nov 2018 for a 4,522-day delay; SC dismissed the last pending appeal, filed by an advocate, 6 Aug 2026 [documented/reported]
Counter-record: the 2005 judgment records that the investigation ran 14 years and cost nearly Rs 250 crore and calls the case a bubble that 'burst'; no conviction in the case [documented]
Case record fields: subject; decision-date and government at the time; first public allegation; investigating body; latest stage; counter-record.

Record (dated): contract 1986-03-24, about ₹1,500 crore; Swedish Radio allegation 1987-04-16; Swiss banks released about 500 documents in 1997 after litigation; Delhi HC 2004-02-04 quashed charges and held the late Prime Minister (1984–89) entitled to be seen as innocent since no trial was possible; Delhi HC 2005-05-31 discharged the Hinduja brothers; Delhi court 2011-03-04 allowed CBI to close the case against the Italian agent, who died 2013-07-12; Supreme Court 2026-08-06 dismissed the final plea [documented for 2004 (judgment opened); reported for the rest (Wikipedia)]

What the record establishes: payments to agents from Bofors were documented in Swiss accounts; receipt by any Indian public servant was never established in any court; the investigation ran 13 years to the 2004 judgment and the matter 39 years to 2026 without a conviction [analytic]

First public allegation: Italian arrest of the Finmeccanica chief 12 Feb 2013 [reported]
Investigating bodies: CBI (FIR 13 Mar 2013; arrest of the former Air Chief 9 Dec 2016; chargesheet Sep 2017; three chargesheets by Feb 2025) and the Enforcement Directorate [reported]

Latest stage in India: extradition of the alleged middleman 4 Dec 2018; SC bail 18 Feb 2025; Delhi HC bail in the ED case 4 Mar 2025; on 23 Dec 2025 the special CBI court noted charges were still not framed after 7 years [reported]
Counter-record: Milan retrial court acquitted the executives 8 Jan 2018; the Italian Court of Cassation upheld the acquittals in 2019 [reported]

What the record establishes: the alleged kickback allocation (≈€30 million, about ₹360 crore, in a middleman's note) is documented as an allegation in the chargesheets; the Italian courts ended in acquittal; no Indian court has reached a verdict in twelve years [analytic]

d: Subject: land at Colaba allotted for a society of war widows and defence personnel; building later occupied by others; Army claimed the land and security risk [documented]
First public allegation: media from 2003; matter prominent Oct 2010; MoEF order of 14 Jan 2011 to demolish (recorded in the 2016 judgment); CBI FIR Jan 2011 [documented/reported]
Investigating bodies: CBI; Judicial Commission (report Apr 2013); CAG (Report No. 11 of 2011 per the CAG portal listing surfaced by search; page unreachable) [reported]

Latest stage: Bombay HC 29 Apr 2016 made the rule absolute (demolition) and stayed it 12 weeks; SC 22 Jul 2016 asked the Centre to take possession and halted demolition; Bombay HC 22 Dec 2017 quashed the Governor's sanction to prosecute a former Chief Minister; appeal and trial pending as of 2024 [documented/reported]
Counter-record: the Society argued delay and laches and that the building had been completed with an Occupation Certificate [documented]
Case record fields: subject; decision-date and government at the time; first public allegation; investigating body; latest stage; counter-record.

Record (dated): Maharashtra appointed a two-member judicial commission under a retired HC judge (J.A. Patil) in January 2011 and CBI began investigating the same month; Bombay HC criticised CBI and ED for slow progress in February–March 2012; CBI arrested eight in March 2012 including two retired Major Generals, a former MLC and IAS officers; the commission's report (April 2013, 182 witnesses; tabled and rejected December 2013) indicted four former Chief Ministers, two former urban-development ministers and 12 bureaucrats and found 25 illegal allotments including 22 benami; the Governor refused sanction to prosecute a former CM in 2013, a later Governor granted it in February 2016 and Bombay HC quashed that sanction 2017-12-22; Bombay HC ordered demolition 2016-04-29; the SC stayed demolition in 2018 and the Army took custody of the building; no final verdict as of 2024 [reported: Wikipedia; commission report and orders not opened]

What the record establishes: a documented finding of irregular allotment by a state commission, no conviction, and a building still standing under judicial stay — the case is about land and allotment, not procurement [analytic]

entities.sub: SC constituted a Technical Committee 27 Oct 2021; Aug 2022: malware in 5 of 29 phones, Pegasus not established; Govt filed only a limited affidavit
entities.publicRole: Court record of the petitions on alleged use of Pegasus on Indian phones.
d: Subject: petitions after July 2021 reports that Pegasus (NSO Group) had targeted Indian phones (NDA government, BJP) [documented]

First public allegation: 18 Jul 2021, a consortium of about 17 news organisations reported alleged Pegasus use based on a list of some 50,000 leaked numbers, nearly 300 reportedly Indian (as recounted in the SC order); earlier Citizen Lab/Amnesty report of 15 Jun 2020 on nine individuals [documented]
Investigating body: Technical Committee of three experts overseen by Justice R V Raveendran (ret.), assisted by Alok Joshi (former Secretary R&AW) and Dr Sundeep Oberoi [documented]
Latest stage: report read out in court 25 Aug 2022; on 29 Apr 2025 the SC declined to make the report public [reported]

Counter-record: the Union filed only a 'limited affidavit' on 16 Aug 2021 citing national security; the court said the State 'does not get a free pass every time the spectre of national security is raised' [documented]
Case record fields: subject; decision-date and government at the time; first public allegation; investigating body; latest stage; counter-record.

Record (dated): Pegasus Project reports from 2021-07-18; IT Minister's statement in Parliament 2021-07-19 ("no factual basis"); Union's limited affidavit 2021-08-16; SC order 2021-10-27 (Ramana CJI, Surya Kant J, Hima Kohli J) constituting a technical committee of three (Chaudhary, Prabaharan, Gumaste) overseen by Justice R.V. Raveendran (retd), holding "national security cannot be the bugbear that the judiciary shies away from, by virtue of its mere mentioning"; committee report considered 2022-08-25: 29 devices examined, malware on 5, no conclusive proof of Pegasus, government did not cooperate; report kept in sealed cover [documented for the 2021 order; reported for the 2022 findings (Wikipedia)]

What the record establishes: that the Union declined to say whether it bought or used Pegasus before the Court; that infection of Indian devices with some spyware was found in a small sample; that attribution to the Indian state was not established by the committee [analytic]

claims.lab: Bofors beside Rafale, identical fields

Rafale (decision 2016, BJP government): first allegation Sep 2018; no investigation ordered by the Court; SC dismissed petitions 2018 and review 2019; CAG Report 3 of 2019 (2.86% below the audit-aligned price; price redacted); convictions: 0. Common feature: an allegation about who the intermediary or offset partner was, answered by the government of the day that it had no role.
claims.innocentReading: The two cases differ in kind: Bofors was a contract with alleged commissions through intermediaries and a criminal chargesheet; Rafale is a government-to-government deal reviewed on petition, with no investigation ordered. Different eras, different statutes (s.17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act since 2018) and an open court file in one, a redacted one in the other.

claims.innocentReading: Chargesheets and framed charges are allegations tested slowly; the absence of a conviction after 7–13 years reflects court delay as much as weakness of evidence, and the Italian acquittals are the only completed trials.

Bofors (1986) predates both. Latest stage of the seven: quashed/discharged (Bofors); petitions dismissed (Rafale); Italian acquittals and Indian trial at pre-charge stage (AgustaWestland); CBI closure report and a separate trial (Tatra); demolition stayed, sanction quashed, appeals pending (Adarsh); court martial outcomes set aside (Sukna); inconclusive, report sealed (Pegasus). claims.innocentReading: Seven hand-picked cases cannot rank two governments: they are the cases that became famous, which depends on the opposition of the day; older cases have had longer to reach a verdict; and a case that ends without conviction is not thereby proved baseless.

narratives.claim: AgustaWestland paid bribes to Indian officials for the VVIP helicopter contract.
narratives.strongestCase: India cancelled the contract in 2014 for integrity-pact breach; a CBI FIR (2013), arrests (2016), chargesheets (2017 onward); an Italian appeal court convicted the executives in 2016 before the conviction was annulled.
narratives.strongestCounter: The Milan retrial court acquitted in 2018 and Cassation upheld the acquittals in 2019; in India charges were still not framed after seven years (Dec 2025); the former Chief's side points to specification changes before his tenure.

narratives.claim: The Tatra/BEML truck purchases were a Rs 750 crore scam.
narratives.strongestCase: A CBI FIR on the Defence Minister's directive (2012), the BEML chairman's suspension, an alleged ~60% mark-up through a middleman, and a separate trial in which charges were framed in 2019 on the alleged Rs 14 crore bribe offer.

narratives.claim: The Government used Pegasus on Indian citizens.
narratives.strongestCase: The Union filed only a 'limited affidavit' and cited national security instead of denying or confirming use; the committee reported the Government did not cooperate; malware was found in 5 of 29 phones; the Court declined in 2025 to release the report.
narratives.strongestCounter: The Technical Committee did not find Pegasus on any of the 29 phones; the Minister told Parliament that unauthorised surveillance does not take place; the Court itself said possessing spyware is not wrong and the question is against whom it is used.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Publication of the committee report, or a forensic attribution of the malware to a state buyer.

narratives.claim: Defence scandals were worse under UPA than under NDA, or the reverse.
narratives.strongestCase: Four of the seven named cases were decided or surfaced under UPA, two under NDA, one earlier; each side's partisans cite the other's cases.
